name: stub_single_instruction_routine
description: A one-instruction routine with no body in the decompiled output. It is called from two places and its address is referenced in two more. The evidence shows nothing beyond that one instruction.

name: stub_clear_target_single_instruction
description: A one-instruction routine whose address is the target of a clear instruction elsewhere. It is called from one place, and its body is too small to show further behaviour.

name: call_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two other routines one after the other and then returns. The seven-instruction body shows no branching, and it is called from one place.

name: call_local_then_fixed_routine
description: Calls one other routine, then a fixed routine at a known address outside this segment, and returns. The decompiled body has no branching and is reached from one place.

name: set_state_with_restore
description: Compares the register input with a stored byte. When they differ, it first writes 255 into the byte, then stores the input, calls two local routines and a fixed external routine, and restores the saved byte. It returns zero after a change and minus one when the value was already current.

name: set_state_if_changed
description: Compares the register input with a stored byte. When they differ, it stores the input, calls two local routines and a fixed external routine, and returns zero. When the value is already current it returns minus one without other work.

name: branch_on_flag_after_change
description: When the register input differs from a stored byte, it stores the input and then chooses one of two call sequences from bit 0 of a flag byte. The first sequence also clears the stored byte twice. It returns zero after a change and minus one otherwise.

name: run_paired_calls_then_clear
description: Runs two pairs of local calls, each pair followed by a fixed external routine, then clears a stored byte twice and returns zero. No arguments are read in the decompiled body.

name: check_disk_image_files
description: Stores two register arguments in globals, then calls library entries at offsets minus 30, 36, 42 and 66 in sequence. The data references the names 1.img and disk1.img. A failed first library check leads to a fixed routine before the return.

name: copy_header_then_walk_records
description: Copies four 32-bit header fields from the input block into the output buffer, then walks a record list. Records with a zero low nibble are copied byte for byte, a nibble of fifteen ends the walk, and any other record is passed to a local routine.

name: relay_single_call_pointer
description: Makes a single call to a local routine and returns. Its own address is taken with a PC-relative load, so it is reached through a pointer rather than direct calls. The decompiled body contains nothing else.

name: forward_to_one_routine
description: Calls one local routine and returns. It is called from one place and has no other work in the decompiled body.

name: store_word_then_call_routine
description: Reads a 16-bit value through the first pointer of its argument block, stores it in the fifth long of that block, then calls one local routine and returns zero.

name: decompress_bitpacked_lz_stream
description: Decodes a bit-packed compressed stream. Flag bits choose between copying a literal run of bytes and copying bytes back from data already written, with lengths and distances read from further bits. Input and output pointers advance until a terminating code.

name: wrap_one_call_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so the body is unknown beyond its seven-instruction size. It is called from five places and makes one call to a local routine. No further behaviour is evidenced.

name: run_chunked_transfer_loop
description: Fills a request block with a callback pointer, two buffer addresses, a size of 32768 and a limit of 65536. It then loops over a length word, calling a local routine for each chunk and advancing the buffer by the amount transferred.

name: advance_fixed_step_counter
description: Stores a result field from the first word of a two-word counter, rounded up to an even number when the second word is zero. It writes the fixed step of 65536 into the next field and advances the counter by one step.

name: set_default_fields_then_call
description: Writes 510 and 16 into two word fields of its structure argument and then calls one local routine.

name: fill_signed_ramp_tables
description: Fills 512 words at a fixed offset from its base. The first 256 words count up from minus 768 in pairs, and the next 256 words count down from minus 2.

name: build_prefix_code_table
description: Counts how many symbols use each code length up to sixteen bits, then computes running offsets for each length. It fills a decode table with symbol values and allocates extra entries for codes longer than the lookup width.

name: decode_bitstream_after_clearing
description: Clears a block of 510 output words, then decodes values from a 16-bit input stream. It refills a bit buffer from input words through local routines whenever the buffer runs out, and calls a fixed routine when the input count is exhausted.

name: decode_bitstream_pair_tables
description: Clears a 510-word output area and decodes a bit-packed stream using a bit buffer refilled from 16-bit input words. Its table handling uses paired entries, and it calls local routines for refills and error paths.

name: advance_bitstream_decoder_state
description: Stores buffer pointers and a count into a decoder state block, then runs a bit-level decode loop over 16-bit input words. It refills the bit buffer through a local routine when the count runs out and returns zero when the input is exhausted.

name: decode_rotate_xor_chain
description: Transforms 32 input bytes into 32 output bytes. Each input byte is rotated left by two bits and XORed with the previous output byte, starting from 255.

name: return_error_code_three
description: Calls one local routine and, when that routine returns a negative result, stores a failure code of 3 in a status field before returning. Otherwise it passes its inputs through.

name: call_library_then_read_status
description: Calls a library entry through a pointer held in the base register, then returns a status word read from a fixed field of the same block.

name: decrement_counter_and_notify
description: Decrements a global counter. When the counter reaches zero, it calls a fixed routine and passes the result to a second fixed routine.

name: init_library_on_first_use
description: Increments a global counter and, on the first increment, calls a library entry at offset minus 198, a fixed routine and a local routine.

name: run_conditional_call_sequence
description: Runs a fixed sequence of local calls. Three of the calls are followed by a second routine that runs only when the preceding call returns a non-negative value.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: A routine whose body is only a return. It is called from one place and performs no other work.

name: run_pair_when_flag_clear
description: Calls two local routines only when a data word holds zero, then returns.

name: stub_return_only_routine
description: A single return instruction found between routines in the segment. No other behaviour is shown.

name: jump_through_vector_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out. The routine is five instructions, is called from two places and passes control through a jump-table entry to a fixed address elsewhere in memory. No further behaviour is evidenced.

name: copy_block_tail_then_call
description: Takes a stored size modulo 512. When the remainder is nonzero, it copies the rest of a 512-byte source block into the output as 32-bit words, then makes two local calls.

name: retry_until_zero_result
description: Repeatedly calls a jump-table entry that passes control to a fixed address, and calls one local routine after each nonzero result, until the result is zero.

name: reset_table_and_poll_ciaa
description: Clears 80 long words in a fixed buffer and copies six 8-byte entries, selected by a counter, into a second buffer. It then checks two status bits of the CIA port A register, which the register notes tie to the fire-button and disk status, before returning.

name: interleave_bitplane_nibbles
description: Converts packed nibble data into bit-plane form by swapping nibble pairs and interleaving bits with mask-and-shift steps. It writes several output bytes per iteration and stops at a fixed buffer end.

name: pack_five_bitplanes
description: Loops over 960 groups of 16 bytes, gathering bits 3 to 7 of each byte into five 16-bit plane words and storing them in order.

name: relay_call_to_local_routine
description: Calls one local routine and returns. The routine is reached through a gap that decodes as code and has no other work.

name: forward_call_then_return
description: Makes one call to a local routine and then returns. The body is otherwise empty.

name: relay_call_gap_routine
description: Calls one local routine and returns. It sits in a gap that decodes as code and has no other work in the decompiled body.

name: relay_call_shared_entry
description: Calls one local routine and returns. Two callers reach it, and its body is otherwise empty.

name: wait_for_video_position
description: Reads the video beam position register and busy-waits until its vertical counter meets a fixed condition, then returns.

name: silence_audio_channels_when_flagged
description: When a flag is set, writes 8192 to a control word and waits for the flag to clear. It then calls four fixed routines and resets four audio volume values to zero. The listed registers are the four audio volume registers and the DMA control register.

name: call_routine_when_flag_clear
description: Calls one fixed routine only when a data word holds zero, then returns.

name: decrement_counter_twice_guarded
description: When a data word is nonzero, decrements a global counter twice and calls a fixed routine each time the counter reaches zero.

name: call_each_entry_until_zero
description: Walks a table of routine entries at a fixed address, calling a local routine for each one until it reaches a zero entry.

name: accumulate_rows_into_nibble_table
description: Walks a list of row pointers, adding each offset into a running 16-bit table and packing the high bits of each sum into nibble fields of an output buffer. It decrements a count in its state block when the list is done, and runs a local routine when a state field equals one.

name: repack_nibble_groups_to_words
description: Repacks groups of four bytes into pairs of 16-bit words for each list entry. Low nibbles are combined into 12-bit values and the remaining nibbles are stored separately.

name: repack_nibbles_with_row_skip
description: Repacks nibble data into 16-bit words for each list entry, moving the output pointer forward at fixed row intervals so that rows are skipped at a regular stride.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Works with the keyboard serial data register. It inverts a stored state flag, shifts the stored code right by one bit, and resets the code to 255 before returning.

name: mix_two_words_into_globals
description: Mixes two 32-bit inputs with shifts, additions and a constant multiply, storing two results in fixed globals and returning the first.

name: fill_long_ramp_stride_160
description: Fills 960 long words at a fixed buffer, each value 160 higher than the previous one, starting from a fixed start value.

name: build_offset_table_from_base
description: Fills a table of pointers at a global address. Each entry is the previous entry plus a global step, starting from a base value minus that step, and the loop stops at the first negative entry.

name: fill_wrapping_offset_table
description: Fills a table of longs with values rising by 768 each step. The value wraps back to its start at a fixed limit, and the loop stops at the first negative entry.

name: fill_wrapping_word_offsets
description: Fills a table of words with values rising by sixteen, wrapping to zero at 304, until the loop reaches a negative entry.

name: collect_active_entry_pointers
description: Scans three tables of entry records and copies the pointer of each record that has a nonzero field and a qualifying flag into a pointer list. The list ends with a zero entry.

name: stamp_fixed_word_before_entries
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of pointers and writes the fixed value 49536 into two words before each entry.

name: return_only_routine_gap
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: clear_buffer_then_run_two
description: Clears 6400 long words at the output address, then makes two local calls and returns.

name: repeat_pair_calls_while_count
description: Calls two local routines in a loop, repeating while a counter field in the structure stays nonnegative.

name: interleave_two_plane_columns
description: Copies a column of words from one source plane and the matching column from a second plane, offset by 10240 bytes, into an output buffer in interleaved pairs with a stride of 40 bytes. A second loop completes the copy for the remaining rows.

name: call_routine_return_zero
description: Calls one local routine and returns zero.

name: build_offset_records_from_list
description: Walks 12-byte source records and builds three-field output records. Each output record holds a running offset that grows by sixteen times the next count, plus copied fields, and the loop ends at the first negative entry.

name: service_four_slots_then_return
description: Calls a fixed routine, then checks four byte slots. For each slot not equal to minus one it calls one local routine, and it finishes with one more call.

name: pass_control_to_routine
description: Calls one local routine and returns. The decompiled body has no other statements.

name: copy_block_and_relocate_header
description: Copies 64 long words of code into a fixed buffer, then checks a four-character signature at the start of the block. When the signature matches, it adds the block base pointer to three offset fields in the header.

name: advance_audio_voice_list
description: Walks a list of audio voice records, decrementing a tick counter for each. When a voice needs a new step, it copies the next period and sample values into the voice record and sets a bit in the channel mask. It returns the index of the last voice processed when the list ends.

name: start_audio_voice_playback
description: Starts a sound on an audio voice. It sets the voice state bits and copies start, length and period values from a sample record, then updates the channel mask and DMA control state. It returns early when a special state byte is set.

name: return_status_six
description: Sets a global status value to 6 and returns the input byte unchanged.

name: service_audio_voices
description: Processes the audio voice list on each tick, applying pending period and sample changes and writing them to the audio channel registers. It also updates the DMA control state and returns a count when the list is finished.

name: set_audio_dma_state_one
description: Clears one state value, sets another global to 1 and writes 255 to a DMA control global, then returns the input byte. The register notes tie DMACON to writes with bit 15 set.

name: clear_dma_state_flags
description: Clears one state byte, sets another to 2, and writes 255 to a global that tracks DMA control, then returns. Value 255 has bit 15 clear, so the write does not set DMA enable bits.

name: copy_block_and_check_header
description: Copies 64 long words of code into a fixed buffer, checks a four-character signature at the start of the block, and then calls four local routines when the header is valid.

name: relocate_offset_entries
description: Adds the block base pointer to three offset fields in a header and to each entry of a following list. It then copies a fixed set of 20 words into a global table.

name: copy_table_and_set_mode
description: Copies 64 long words from a table into a buffer when a flag is set and clears the flag. It then sets a global from a chain of sentinel checks, with priorities from eight down to one, and finally writes 49152 to an interrupt control value. The register notes tie bit 15 writes to enabling interrupts.

name: return_input_byte
description: Returns its input byte unchanged, with no other work in the decompiled body.

name: stub_repeated_slot_code
description: A single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the four-slot service code shown elsewhere. The repeated body is probably a decoding artefact, so only its address reference and its callers are reliable.

name: service_four_slots_with_tail
description: Continues the four-slot service pattern: calls a fixed routine, checks four byte slots and calls one local routine for each slot not equal to minus one, then makes a final call. It is a longer copy of the same sequence reached from a second entry.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the four-slot service code shown elsewhere. The repeated body is probably a decoding artefact, so only its address reference and its callers are reliable.

name: stub_repeated_slot_body
description: A single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the four-slot service sequence seen elsewhere. The repeated body is probably a decoding artefact, so only its address reference and its two callers are reliable.

name: service_four_slots_alt_entry
description: Its decompiled body is the same four-slot service sequence seen at other entries: it calls a fixed routine, checks four byte slots and calls one local routine for each slot not equal to minus one. The match rests on the pseudo-code alone, and the register facts add nothing further. It is reached through a PC-relative load.

name: snapshot_registers_when_flagged
description: When a flag is set, it calls a local routine and stores the input data and address register values into fixed globals, then calls two more routines.

name: advance_audio_channel_location
description: Advances a sample index counter and, on wrap-around, resets it and handles a pending flag. It then sets the channel 0 location register from a table entry. The routine touches the channel 0 location register.

name: dispatch_sequence_command_nibble
description: Reads the low nibble of a sequence word and switches on it. The period value is updated and clamped to a minimum of 113 before being stored. The decompiled output is partial, so only the period update and the nibble switch are shown.

name: step_voice_record_pointers
description: Copies one value into a voice record and advances two pointers by stride values held in registers, repeating until a count reaches its end. The decompiled body is partial.

name: process_voice_sequence_state
description: Processes four voice records on each tick. While a delay count is nonzero it decrements the count and returns; otherwise it reads the next sequence entry for each active voice and copies its values into the voice record.

name: reenable_audio_interrupts
description: When a flag is set and a pending word is nonzero, clears the pending word, stores a value into a channel record, waits for a status loop and writes 49152 to an interrupt control value. The register notes say that bit 15 writes enable interrupts.

name: update_channel_limit_countdown
description: Decrements a countdown byte and, when it reaches zero, calls a routine and clears the countdown. Otherwise it computes a six-bit index, updates channel limit variables and writes to the channel 0 location register.

name: stub_return_in_gap
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: init_audio_channel_state
description: Initialises a five-word audio channel record with fixed values and writes constants to the channel volume and interrupt control globals. It returns the input value merged with a fixed constant. The register notes tie the writes to the audio volume and DMA control registers.

name: clear_flag_and_store_word
description: When a RAM flag is set, clears a counter and the flag, zeroes a second field and stores the input word in a third field. Otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: check_sample_ready_state
description: Checks a busy flag and a special value in a table entry indexed by the current channel number. When the entry is minus one it sets a flag and returns. For entries other than minus two it calls one local routine and increments a counter; otherwise it advances the index.

name: start_channel_three_sample
description: Starts playback on audio channel 3 by setting its volume, period, length and location registers from a sample record, with DMA and interrupt control writes. It then calls two routines.

name: double_value_when_all_set
description: When three flag values are all nonzero, doubles a global value and stores it back. Otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: initialise_record_from_input
description: Zeroes a 58-long record and copies a list of fields from the input structure into it, including values at fixed offsets from the record base.

name: service_pointer_list_with_dma
description: Walks a list of pointers and increments a counter for each entry, wrapping at 300. It writes 9961472 into the first long of each entry and updates a flag before calling one local routine. The facts list the DMA control register.

name: stub_bad_instruction_halt
description: Decoding stops at this point with a bad-instruction marker, so the entry holds no usable code. It is referenced by an absolute test and has one caller.

name: stub_bad_data_pcrel_entry
description: Decoding stops at this point with a bad-instruction marker, so the entry holds no usable code. It is referenced by a PC-relative load and has one caller.

name: set_custom_chip_registers_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available. The routine is 51 instructions, touches two custom chip register offsets and calls one routine. No further behaviour is evidenced.

name: stub_timeout_single_instruction
description: A one-instruction routine with no decompiled body, because the decompiler timed out. It is called only from a move-quick return stub, and no further behaviour is evidenced.

name: return_only_executed_stub
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_b
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_c
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_d
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_e
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_f
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_g
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: return_only_executed_stub_h
description: A single return instruction reached during the reference run. It is entered from outside the static flow and performs no other work.

name: initialise_program_entry_state
description: Program entry point. It clears several state globals, records the start context and a stack value, and calls a library routine. When a task field is zero it sets a status value and calls two more library routines before a final call.

name: handle_task_message_port
description: Uses task and message port calls. It finds the current task, sets its priority, waits on a port, reads messages and replies to them. Library open and close routines and a copper-list free call are also listed in its calls.

name: open_dos_file_with_retry
description: Calls a sequence of DOS library entries inside a loop. It tries a lock step and an open step, unlocks on failure, and closes the Workbench screen beforehand. The hardware note lists the DMA control register.

name: return_only_handler_stub
description: A single return instruction reached through a handler pointer stored in data. It performs no other work.

name: load_screen_file_from_disk
description: Calls routines to load a screen file from the disk path named in the text data. When the first check reports a failure, it sets up the request block and makes a further call. Otherwise it makes three follow-up calls and returns.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three routines in order and returns. The four-instruction body has no branching.

name: advance_seed_and_shift
description: Multiplies a 16-bit state word stored in the caller's structure by 31415, adds one, stores the result back, and returns it shifted right by a count from a register. It is a simple pseudo-random step.

name: return_only_called_stub
description: A single return instruction reached by a call from one place. It performs no other work.

name: install_interrupt_servers
description: Clears several state words and stores pointers into interrupt setup fields. It then calls library routines to add an interrupt server and set an interrupt vector, and writes fixed values into setup fields before returning.

name: remove_interrupt_servers
description: Calls library entries to remove an interrupt server and restore an interrupt vector. It sets two globals to 1920 and 15, then restores four saved words before returning. The hardware notes list the DMA control and interrupt enable registers.

name: return_only_gap_stub
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: read_joystick_position_delta
description: Reads the joystick data register and the fire-button port, computes the change from the previous reading, and accumulates a damped position value. Four routines are called from its body. The register notes tie the fire-button port to the joystick and mouse buttons and disk status.

name: return_only_gap_routine_b
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: process_keyboard_serial_input
description: Inverts a keyboard serial byte and removes its release bit. It then looks up a translated character, or sets a special return value for two reserved codes, and calls routines to store the result in a ring buffer.

name: set_flag_bit_one
description: Clears bit one of a flag word when the input has bit seven set, and sets it otherwise. It returns with no other work.

name: set_flag_bit_zero
description: Clears bit zero of a flag word when the input has bit seven set, and sets it otherwise. It returns with no other work.

name: or_word_into_flag_state
description: ORs its input word into a global flag word and returns.

name: append_key_to_ring_buffer
description: When the input has bit seven clear, looks up a translated value for the key code, adjusted by a flag bit, and appends it to a ring buffer. The write index wraps at its limit.

name: check_ring_buffer_empty
description: Returns zero when the read and write indices of a ring buffer are equal and minus one otherwise. Callers can use it to test whether input is waiting.

name: read_ring_buffer_byte
description: Busy-waits until the ring buffer read index differs from the write index, then returns the byte there and advances the read index with wrap-around.

name: handle_audio_channel_zero_interrupt
description: Audio channel zero interrupt handler. It writes the channel's sample bits, then either decrements a per-channel counter and writes a combined value, or resets the counter to its maximum and writes the channel's request bit to the interrupt value.

name: decrement_audio_channel_zero_counter
description: Decrements the channel zero counter and writes 1 to the DMA control global.

name: handle_audio_channel_one_interrupt
description: Audio channel one interrupt handler. It writes the channel's sample bits, then either decrements a per-channel counter and writes a combined value, or resets the counter to its maximum and writes the channel's request bit to the interrupt value.

name: decrement_audio_channel_one_counter
description: Decrements the channel one counter and writes 2 to the DMA control global.

name: handle_audio_channel_two_interrupt
description: Audio channel two interrupt handler. It writes the channel's sample bits, then either decrements a per-channel counter and writes a combined value, or resets the counter to its maximum and writes the channel's request bit to the interrupt value.

name: decrement_audio_channel_two_counter
description: Decrements the channel two counter and writes 4 to the DMA control global.

name: handle_audio_channel_three_interrupt
description: Audio channel three interrupt handler. It writes the channel's sample bits, then either decrements a per-channel counter and writes a combined value, or resets the counter to its maximum and writes the channel's request bit to the interrupt value.

name: decrement_audio_channel_three_counter
description: Decrements the channel three counter and writes 8 to the DMA control global.

name: ramp_audio_volume_toward_target
description: Writes the current volume to each audio volume register whose bit is set in a mask. It then steps the shared volume value up or down by one per call, stopping at zero or at sixty-three.

name: accumulate_cia_timer_delta
description: Reads a timer byte from the CIA chip, computes its change since the previous call with wrap-around correction, and adds four times that change to a running total.

name: allocate_even_offset_slot
description: Rounds its input up to an even value and adds it to a base index. When the result is below a limit it stores the new index and returns an offset from a stored base. Otherwise it returns minus one.

name: retry_memory_allocation_countdown
description: Retries a memory allocation through the exec library in a countdown loop. The time budget is chosen from one of two constants and reduced in steps of 1000 between attempts. It writes a message through DOS when a flag is set.

name: set_up_display_colormap
description: Checks a status pair and an index, then calls graphics library routines to obtain a colour map. It stores the colour map pointer and display list values into globals and calls two local routines.

name: load_pitback_artwork_once
description: When a state word is zero, calls one local routine to load the PitBack artwork named in the text data, then clears a second state word and sets the first to minus one.

name: load_mirror_artwork_once
description: When a state word is zero, calls one local routine to load the Mirror artwork named in the text data, then sets the state word to minus one and clears a second state word.

name: record_timed_sample_request
description: Stores a 12-byte request record with its index and a running counter, then calls a local routine for a count and adds it to the running total. It returns half the count while the total stays within a limit of 37701, and minus one otherwise.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns minus one and performs no other work. It is called from one place and sits in a gap between routines.

name: load_sound_bank_files
description: Calls two local routines and, when a flag is set, calls two more. The text data names the Sounds file in the PDData directory.

name: load_second_sound_bank
description: When a flag is set, calls two local routines. The text data names the second sound file, Sounds2, in the PDData directory.

name: relocate_sound_table_entries
description: Calls one local routine, then adds a base pointer to the first long of each of 30 three-long records. The text data names the Sounds3 file.

name: relocate_table_entries_from_base
description: Adds a base pointer to the first long of each of 30 three-long records, starting from the table address it receives.

name: flip_byte_sign_bits
description: Gets a count from one local routine, then adds 128 to each byte of a run at a stored pointer, which flips the top bit of each byte. It then calls one more routine.

name: store_handle_and_call_library
description: Calls a local routine that returns a pair of values. When the second value is zero it returns minus one. Otherwise it stores that value and calls library entries in sequence before returning.

name: read_dos_file_block
description: Calls a local routine for a value pair and returns minus one when the value is zero. Otherwise it stores the value as a file handle, calls DOS library entries to seek, read and close, and returns the result of a further routine.

name: return_only_gap_routine_c
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: read_demo_lap_file
description: Calls one local routine to get a file handle. When the handle is nonzero, it stores it and calls DOS library entries to read and close the file, returning zero. Otherwise it returns minus one. The text data names the Demo.Lap file.

name: read_high_scores_table
description: Gets a file handle from a local routine, reads the high scores table through DOS library entries, and closes the file. The text data names the HighScores.Tab file in the PDData directory.

name: write_high_scores_table
description: Stores a file handle from a local routine and writes the table through DOS library entries. When the first byte of the buffer is an asterisk, it writes an extra block. It closes the file and returns zero, or minus one when the open step fails.

name: xor_buffer_in_place
description: XORs 220 bytes in place, starting at a buffer pointer, with the constant 42.

name: read_file_in_steps
description: Opens a file through a local routine and reads it through DOS library entries in several steps, closing it at the end. Most of its body consists of library calls.

name: load_file_with_read_steps
description: Loads a file by calling DOS library read and close entries in sequence, after a local routine has returned a valid handle. It returns zero on success and minus one when the handle is missing.

name: read_file_and_offset_records
description: Opens a file through a local routine, reads it through DOS library entries, and adds a stored base value to each long of a counted list of records.

name: build_bobs_path_name
description: Copies seven characters of an eight-character name into a path buffer, turning spaces into zero bytes, then calls one local routine with the result. The text data names the PDBOBS directory.

name: store_result_in_indexed_slot
description: Calls one local routine and, when the index is nonnegative, stores the returned value in the table slot selected by that index.

name: copy_bobs_name_and_call
description: Copies seven characters of an eight-character name into the PDBOBS path buffer, mapping spaces to zero bytes, then calls one local routine.

name: load_bob_library_entries
description: Runs a long sequence of loading steps for the BobLib artwork file in the PDArtwork directory. It calls a local routine after each step and stops early when a step returns a negative value, then closes the file through the DOS library.

name: load_top_racer_bobs
description: Sets an offset global from two positions, calls two local routines and returns the first routine's result. The text data names the TopRacer0 and TopRacer0TP bob files.

name: load_inset_bob_file
description: Sets an offset global from two positions, then calls one local routine and stores its result. The text data names the Inset bob file.

name: load_tv_and_banner_bobs
description: Sets display position values from a base offset of 14000 and a span of 16000 when a flag is clear, otherwise adjusts an offset from the current value. It then calls local routines for the TVBack artwork and the Banner and TeeVee bob files.

name: load_bob_library_second_part
description: Runs a sequence of loading steps for the BobLib2 artwork file. It calls a local routine after each step and stops early when a step returns a negative value, then closes the file through the DOS library.

name: run_sequence_with_special_case
description: Loops over a counter that starts from a value returned by a local routine, calling a sequence of routines for each value. For the value 12345 it saves and restores one structure field around the calls.

name: build_index_table_64
description: Fills a 64-entry table of longs in two nested loops. Each entry is four times the row index plus a value read from a table with a stride of 24 bytes.

name: store_pair_and_call_routine
description: Stores its two register inputs into a pair of globals and calls one local routine.

name: store_inputs_and_close_file
description: Stores two register inputs into globals, then calls one local routine to get a handle. When the handle is nonzero it stores it, calls a routine, closes the file through DOS and returns that result. Otherwise it calls one more routine and returns zero.

name: load_image_bitmap_from_file
description: Seeks and reads image data through DOS library entries, initialises a graphics bitmap, and calls four local routines to fill the bitmap rows.

name: walk_linked_record_pair
description: When a stored record pointer is set, reads a status value through the DOS library, computes a count from a stored step, and walks two linked records, copying pointer values and calling two local routines.

name: match_iff_chunk_tag
description: Compares the four-character chunk tag at its input against six known IFF chunk names: FORM, ILBM, BMHD, CMAP, GRAB and BODY. It returns the index of the match, or minus one when none matches.

name: repeat_four_calls_with_extra
description: Repeats a fixed series of four local calls for a counted run, adding a fifth call on each pass when a global value is above four.

name: decode_signed_run_length_bytes
description: Decodes a run-length byte stream. A negative count repeats the following byte, a positive count copies that many literal bytes, and a marker value ends the sequence. Output advances through a destination pointer as it is written.

name: load_cockpit_artwork
description: When a flag is clear, calls one local routine and returns. Otherwise it sets a flag byte and calls one local routine. The text data names the Cockpit artwork.

name: advance_cockpit_offset_row
description: Calls one local routine, then adds 116 to a stored offset. The text data names the Cockpit artwork.

name: fill_byte_and_word_tables
description: Fills two byte buffers from repeated calls to a local routine, looping over a full 16-bit count, then fills a word buffer the same way.

name: init_bitmap_plane_pointers
description: Initialises a graphics bitmap structure through a library entry, then computes four plane pointers in steps of a base size. It clears the bitmap through a blitter-clear library stub.

name: setup_display_view_and_viewport
description: Initialises the graphics view, rastport and viewport through library entries. It frees older viewport copper lists first, then builds new copper lists with the MakeVPort and MrgCop entries and loads the view.

name: rebuild_display_view_state
description: Sets a view state and a mode value of five, allocates a view structure when none exists, then calls library entries that build the view and viewport copper lists with a width of 320.

name: build_and_load_copper_view
description: Sets a view flag to one and a mode value to five, then calls library entries that make a viewport, merge the copper list and load the view.

name: load_view_with_mode_four
description: Clears the view flag, sets the mode value to four and calls the library LoadView entry.

name: update_clamped_step_value
description: Stores the current counter and computes its change from the previously stored value, clamped between 8 and 50, into a field. It calls two local routines and makes further calls when a field is nonzero.

name: reset_view_and_clear_flag
description: Calls one local routine, calls the library LoadView entry and clears a state byte.

name: free_view_copper_lists
description: Copies four stored view values to backup fields, frees copper lists and viewport copper lists through library entries, then calls local routines depending on a flag and loads the view again.

name: build_first_viewport_copper
description: Clears two list pointers and two values, then calls the library MakeVPort and MrgCop entries and saves the two resulting values.

name: build_second_viewport_copper
description: Clears two list pointers and two values, then calls the library MakeVPort and MrgCop entries and saves the two resulting values into a second pair of fields.

name: release_and_reload_view_lists
description: Copies two saved view fields, calls library entries that free the copper lists and viewport lists, and reloads the view. It frees the old list objects when their pointers have changed.

name: check_hunk_type_code
description: Compares values against AmigaDOS hunk type codes, which the executable loader uses when it processes sections. The decompiled body is large and partly unreliable, so only the comparison step is evidenced.

name: reset_state_run_four_calls
description: Clears a state word and calls four local routines in sequence.

name: forward_arguments_to_routine
description: Calls one local routine, then calls a second routine with its register arguments passed through, and returns its first two register inputs unchanged.

name: checksum_byte_range
description: Sums the bytes of a memory range that runs from a start address up to a fixed end address, and returns the total.

name: store_call_result_in_field
description: Calls one local routine and stores its result in a field of the structure.

name: check_hunk_header_codes
description: Compares values with AmigaDOS hunk type codes used by the executable loader, then calls two local routines. The five-instruction body is partly unreliable in the decompiled output, so only the comparison and the two calls are evidenced.

name: return_only_gap_routine_d
description: A single return instruction found in a gap between routines. No other behaviour is shown.

name: store_fixed_constant_global
description: Stores the fixed 32-bit constant 1986840924 into a global and returns. The code alone does not show how the value is used elsewhere.
